stem: Let $X=\{1, 2, 3\}$. The relation $R=\{(1, {=p}), (2, {=q}), (3, {=c}), (1, {=s}k+{=r})\}$ is from $X$ to the set of natural numbers. Find the value of $k$ for which $R$ is a function.
solution: Each of 1, 2 and 3 appears once as a first projection except 1, which appears in the pairs $(1, {=p})$ and $(1, {=s}k+{=r})$.
For R to be a function, 1 must have only one second projection, so ${=s}k+{=r}={=p}$.
